status_summary: The FCC has acted on one media ownership rule, the 39 percent national television ownership cap, but the order is not shown to be in effect. On 2026-08-06 the Commission voted 2-1 to repeal the cap in favor of case-by-case review of transactions, through Report and Order FCC 26-53 in MB Docket 17-318; the FCC's own release gives no effective date. Trade press accounts tie the effective date to publication but differ on whether and when publication occurred, and a Federal Register search for FCC rules after 2026-08-07 found no publication of the order. In early October 2026 a group of state and regional cable associations asked the FCC to reconsider, stay and enjoin the repeal pending judicial review, and said they would seek a court stay if the FCC does not act; no court case was reported filed. Commissioner Gomez dissented, saying only Congress can change the cap, and Free Press has said it plans to appeal. On the wider rules review, the FCC has run a Delete, Delete, Delete proceeding that has published a series of rules removing outdated regulations since 2025-08-04, including one on 2026-06-22; no action on other media ownership rules was found.

timeline.event: The Media Bureau publishes a request for updated comment on whether to change, keep or eliminate the 39 percent national audience reach cap and the UHF discount (MB Docket 17-318).

The FCC publishes the first final rules in its Delete, Delete, Delete proceeding, removing outdated, obsolete and unnecessary regulations and changing delegated authority for deletions exempt from notice and comment; further deletion rules follow, including on 2025-08-20, 2025-12-12 and 2026-01-14 (Federal Register lists 44 FCC documents mentioning the proceeding since 2025-01-20).
The FCC publishes a rule titled Deletion of Obsolete Regulations, which removes outdated rules, including some in the broadcast part of its regulations.

An FCC press release announces an order to replace the 39 percent national television ownership cap with case-by-case review, weighing localism, viewpoint diversity and competition where relevant, with a vote set for 2026-08-06.
A Federal Register Sunshine Act notice lists a Report and Order amending the National Television Multiple Ownership Rule (47 CFR 73.3555(e), MB Docket 17-318) for the 2026-08-06 meeting.

The FCC adopts, by a 2-1 vote (Chairman Carr and Commissioner Trusty in favor, Commissioner Gomez dissenting), Report and Order FCC 26-53 in MB Docket 17-318 repealing the 39 percent national television multiple ownership rule and replacing it with case-by-case review in which the agency approves deals that serve the public interest; the FCC's news release calls it the first change to the rule in over 20 years and states no effective date. Commissioner Gomez's dissent argues that the Consolidated Appropriations Act of 2004 fixed the cap in statute so only Congress can change it. Free Press says it plans to appeal (per Axios).
NewscastStudio reports the order takes effect after Federal Register publication, that Gomez argued only Congress can change the cap, and that Carr expects a court challenge.

Ten state and regional cable associations file a petition with the FCC asking it to reconsider the repeal and to stay and enjoin it pending judicial review; they say they will treat a lack of FCC action by the Federal Register publication date as a denial and seek a stay from a federal appeals court.

title: Eliminate dated FCC media ownership rules and review FCC rules for repeal
uncertainties: The FCC news release of 2026-08-06 was opened by direct fetch this pass and confirms the action, vote, order number, docket and the absence of an effective date. The Commissioner Gomez statement was opened and read by the independent reviewer; it is a dissent and says only Congress can raise or remove the cap. The adopted Report and Order text itself was not read, so the case-by-case test, any treatment of the UHF discount and the effective-date clause are unverified. Reports conflict on timing: one trade outlet says the order was published on 2026-10-01 and another (Light Reading, citing an FCC document) says 2026-10-02 with effect 60 days later; these may refer to the FCC release of the full text rather than the Federal Register, which I could not confirm. A Federal Register query for FCC rules published after 2026-08-07 mentioning ownership returned only an unrelated FM auction notice, so the order appeared unpublished, but the index may lag. Inference: if publication were on 2026-10-02 the effective date would fall about 2026-12-01, but no Federal Register date is established. The petition filing date is reported as 2026-10-02 (a Friday) by Light Reading and as a Tuesday of that week by another outlet, so the exact day is uncertain. No court filing was found. No Federal Register document on local ownership rules or the top-four prohibition was found; a Unified Agenda entry for broadcast ownership rules (Federal Register 2026-08-14) was seen but not read in detail. Other Delete, Delete, Delete deletions were seen but not individually checked. The Mandate's universal service point on p.857 is not assessed here.
